title: Traffic-weighted probe scheduler and graceful-throttle rollout guard
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: reduce false-positive regressions during short traffic bursts by making canary probing schedule traffic-aware and by providing a graceful throttle-based rollout guard. This PR implements a traffic-weighted probe scheduler that samples probe windows proportional to recent route weights and a graceful-throttle rollout guard that scales back probe intensity and gracefully reduces canary traffic when pressure is detected. The scheduler avoids over-sampling low-volume routes and concentrates signal where unit economics matter, while the guard prevents oscillatory rollbacks by enforcing a decay window and a max-throttle-per-interval. Changes include a new scheduling service, metric plumbing for per-route weight signals, heuristics for probe cadence (min/max cadence, jitter), a throttle controller with PID-like smoothing, and a canary policy extension to opt routes into traffic-weighted probing. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged for routes not opted-in. Testing: unit tests for scheduling heuristics, integration tests with simulated traffic shapes, and an internal canary run on staging for 48 hours. Rollout plan: staged canary to 10% of perf-canary agents then full roll after 72h with no false-positive regressions. Impact: expected to reduce noise from tail bursts and decrease unnecessary rollbacks by focusing detection on economically meaningful traffic. See linked Linear items for evaluation criteria and alert thresholds.

review_thread: Diego Morales: Overall this looks promising. Can you clarify how probe weight is computed for routes with very sparse traffic?

Aisha Khan: We compute a 5m EWMA of route qps and then normalize against the 95th percentile across routes to avoid domination by noisy spikes. For routes below a low-QPS threshold we use a floor and opt to run probes at a minimum cadence so we still get coverage.
Priya Iyer: The PID-like smoothing is clever but we should avoid high oscillation on rapid ramp-ups. Add a separate ramp-rate limiter?
Aisha Khan: Added a ramp-rate limiter with configurable rate_per_min in the controller and unit tests cover ramp scenarios.
Samir Patel: CI failed once on integration due to a timing assumption in the simulated harness. Please make the timing tolerant and re-run.
Aisha Khan: Fixed timing window and made harness deterministic by seeding the RNG. Re-ran integration tests and pushed fix.
Priya Iyer: Approved after docs and runbook updates. Marking as ready to merge.
Diego Morales: LGTM. Recommend a staged rollout and a post-mortem template for unexpected rollbacks.
